This is huge. Now they know how memories are stored and how we access them later? I imagine it's probably not long off that we read about someone successfully implanting a fake memory.

Well, we already know how to trick people into forming false memories by associating false memories with real ones. Memories are basically instructions for the brain to relive the event or information using the same structures that generate the memories in the first place. The result is that the memories are open to being edited or modified by any new information. You can read a bit about it here: http://www.washington.edu/news/2001/06/11/i-tawt-i-taw-a-bunny-wabbit-at-disneyland-new-evidence-shows-false-memories-can-be-created/

It really isn't. The idea of a memory "engram" has been around for a while now, and most of the work done in this study is fairly common-place these days. The only real significance seems to stem from the fact that they continuously tracked these structures.

I'm a bit surprised to see publications like Wired even being accepted in this subreddit. They're as popsci as popsci gets.
